workload: Standard production linked QEMU/RPi5 images against published 1ddb61f2 and the existing bounded DDB process-copy workload. No allocation, payload, pool metadata, retention or occupancy changes; previous endpoint evidence is reused only for these unchanged boundaries. Image allocation and page reservation are measured separately.
assessment: Adopt indexed linear-struct context-change checking and the complete machine-stop admission/resume boundary. llvm-size read-only allocation grows by 64 bytes on each platform; data/BSS and image reservation are unchanged (QEMU 2392064 bytes; RPi5 5308416). No new pin, lock, runtime generation field or reclamation counter. This is local compile-time exclusion, not proof of remote CPU quiescence, diagnostic pool derivation, or physical cache/timing safety. Remaining diagnostic escapes are explicitly retained as unfinished lifetime work, not renamed as removed.
next_trigger: Measure again when diagnostic pool access or fatal-console authority changes, a new lifetime/resource is introduced, or the full safe-memory stage completes. Repeat cross-OS measurements only when its normalized boundary changes.
